lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4 you met lines and shapes. What are parallel lines? Lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
Shapes belong to families. Every quadrilateral has 4 straight sides. Some quadrilaterals have more special properties.
A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides. A rectangle is a parallelogram with 4 right angles. A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides.
A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus: it has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. So every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.

Triangles are sorted by their sides (equilateral: 3 equal; isosceles: 2 equal; scalene: none equal) and by their angles (right: one is 90°; obtuse: one is more than 90°; acute: all are less than 90°).
Try it in the world: build a square, a rectangle and a rhombus from blocks in your world. Which one belongs to all three families at once? Next: angles in triangles and quadrilaterals.

exercises.hint: Does a square have 4 right angles?
exercises.explain: True: a square has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle.

exercises.hint: Do all rectangles have 4 equal sides?
exercises.explain: False: a rectangle doesn't always have 4 equal sides.

exercises.prompt: How many sides does every quadrilateral have?
Which shape is both a rectangle and a rhombus?
A triangle can have two right angles.
exercises.hint: A triangle's angles add up to 180°.
exercises.explain: False: 90° + 90° = 180°, leaving nothing for the third angle.

exercises.prompt: A shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles. What is it?
exercises.explain: A rhombus has 4 equal sides; with right angles it would be a square.

exercises.prompt: Can a triangle be both right and isosceles?
Which shapes always have 2 pairs of parallel sides?
exercises.explain: Every parallelogram (and so every rectangle, rhombus and square) has 2 pairs.

exercises.hint: Is the rhombus below the parallelogram in the tree?
exercises.explain: True: a rhombus has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

exercises.prompt: Sort the shapes: always a parallelogram, or not always?
exercises.hint: Does it always have 2 pairs of parallel sides?
exercises.explain: Squares, rectangles and rhombuses always have 2 pairs of parallel sides: parallelograms. Kites and trapeziums don't.

exercises.prompt: Match each triangle to its description.
exercises.explain: Equilateral: 3 equal sides. Isosceles: 2 equal sides. Scalene: none equal.

exercises.prompt: Sort the triangles by their sides.
exercises.hint: Count how many sides have the same length: 3, 2 or none?
exercises.explain: Equilateral, 3 equal sides: 5, 5, 5 and 9, 9, 9. Isosceles, 2 equal: 4, 4, 6 and 7, 7, 2. Scalene, none equal: 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 9.

exercises.prompt: Sort the triangles by their angles.
exercises.hint: Look for a 90° angle, then for one more than 90°; if there is neither, all are less than 90°.
exercises.explain: Right, with a 90° angle: 90, 45, 45 and 90, 60, 30. Obtuse, with one over 90°: 120, 30, 30 and 100, 50, 30. Acute, all under 90°: 60, 60, 60 and 70, 60, 50. Each adds up to 180°.
